details: RLVR training of multiple heterogeneous LLM agents on the same task is done in isolation, so each agent's expensive verified rollouts are used only for self-training; the paper formalizes Heterogeneous Agent Collaborative RL (HACRL): collaborative optimization via cross-agent rollout sharing with strictly independent execution at inference, i.e. bidirectional mutual learning rather than one-way teacher-to-student distillation or coupled multi-agent execution.

HACPO: a group-based policy-optimization algorithm where each agent's objective sums a self-rollout term and a cross-agent-rollout term, with heterogeneity handled by (i) a capability-ratio-weighted advantage baseline over all agents' rewards, (ii) capability-ratio scaling of gradients from other agents' samples, (iii) sequence-level (length-normalized, cross-tokenizer) importance ratios reweighted by a stop-gradient exponential factor, and (iv) asymmetric, within-step progressively tightened clipping for cross-agent ratios.

Theoretical claim: the oracle capability-aware baseline is unbiased (expected value equals the learner agent's expected reward), with high-probability error bounds for its finite-batch empirical version.
Training: 7.5k high-quality math questions from MATH; max prompt 1024 / response 4096 tokens.
Evaluation: MATH-500, MATH, GSM8K, AIME2025, AMC23, Minerva, OlympiadBench (max response 8196 for main tables).
Heterogeneous model: Qwen3-4B-Base + Llama3.2-3B-Instruct (cross-tokenizer via detokenize/retokenize; also Qwen3-1.7B-Base + Llama3.2-1B-Instruct). Six combinations total.
verl framework, 8 GPUs, one epoch, lr 1e-6, batch 128, mini-batch 64, G=8 rollouts per prompt.

Self-rollout clipping follows GSPO (eps_low 3e-4, eps_high 4e-4); cross-agent clipping lower bound 1-delta ≈ 0.8-0.9 with per-update tightening delta_step 0.01-0.025; exponential IS alpha typically 1 (up to 3).
Single-agent GRPO and GSPO (same rollout cost, half the updates).
GSPO×2: single-agent GSPO with double rollouts (n=16, mini-batch 32) and double updates — matched updates, double rollout cost; plus a GSPO updates×2 variant for runtime comparison.
Naive: two agents sharing rollouts without any of HACPO's four mechanisms.
KD and MARL intentionally omitted as differently formulated.
Removal of capability-aware advantage estimation; removal of capability coefficient in gradient modulation; sweep of alpha in {0,1,2,3}; removal of clipping and of the stepwise schedule.
Five random seeds on Qwen3-1.7B/4B-Base; runtime and peak GPU memory profiling; measurement of cross-agent vs self importance ratio statistics.

key_findings.finding: HACPO improves all participating heterogeneous agents and beats a double-rollout single-agent GSPO baseline at half the rollout cost.
key_findings.evidence: Average accuracy over 7 benchmarks improves by +3.6% on average over GSPO×2; e.g. Qwen3-4B 0.755 vs 0.691, Qwen3-4B-Instruct 0.818 vs 0.799, Qwen3-1.7B-Base 0.493 vs 0.465, Llama3.2-3B 0.390 vs 0.334; gains hold across all six model pairs and three heterogeneity types.

key_findings.finding: Naive rollout sharing without heterogeneity-aware corrections is actively harmful, often falling below no-training or single-agent baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Naive two-agent sharing gives 0.583 for Qwen3-4B (vs 0.635 untrained, 0.684 GSPO) and 0.691 for 4B-Instruct (vs 0.799 GSPO); similar degradations in the size and cross-model settings.

key_findings.finding: Mutual learning is bidirectional: even a clearly weaker agent improves the stronger one, so gains are not mere distillation.
key_findings.evidence: In the heterogeneous-state pair the already-strong Qwen3-4B-Instruct gains +1.9% over GSPO×2 while the weaker 4B gains +6.4%; in the Qwen3-4B-Base + Llama3.2-3B pair both improve (0.597 and 0.390) despite large capability and architecture gaps.

key_findings.finding: Each of the four mechanisms is necessary, with the capability-aware baseline and stepwise clipping most critical.
key_findings.evidence: Removing capability-aware advantage estimation drops averages from 0.493 to 0.465 (1.7B) and 0.601 to 0.586 (4B); removing the capability coefficient in gradient modulation gives 0.462/0.600; removing clipping causes severe training instability while a static bound converges suboptimally; optimal alpha is combination-dependent (0 clearly worse, e.g. 0.63 vs 0.664 on MATH500).

key_findings.finding: The capability-aware baseline is provably unbiased in the oracle case with bounded finite-batch error.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem shows E[mu*] equals the learner's expected reward (hence zero-mean centered advantage), and Hoeffding plus union bounds give error O((4/gamma^2 + 1/gamma)(sqrt(log(4n/delta)/2B) + sqrt(log(4n/delta)/2BG))) for the empirical ratio-based baseline.
